title: Devissage of a property of coherent sheaves over the integral closed subschemes of a Noetherian scheme
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme], i.e. locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], and let $\mathcal P$ be a property of coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules [pqf-def-coherent]. For a sheaf of ideals $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ and an $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal G$ [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] let $\mathcal J\mathcal G\subseteq\mathcal G$ be the image of the multiplication map $\mathcal J\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G\to\mathcal G$ [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]; stalks $\mathcal G_x$ are as in [def-weil-pbc-module-stalk], $\mathfrak m_x\subset\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is the maximal ideal of the local ring [def-weil-residue-field], and $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal G)=\{x\in X:\mathcal G_x\neq0\}$ [def-weil-pbc-closed-subset-proper-over-base](2). Assume: (0) $\mathcal P$ holds for the zero module; (1) for every short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal F_1\to\mathcal F\to\mathcal F_2\to0$ of coherent $\mathcal O_X$-modules, if $\mathcal F_1$ and $\mathcal F_2$ have $\mathcal P$ then so has $\mathcal F$; (2) if $\mathcal F$ is coherent and $\mathcal P$ holds for $\mathcal F^{\oplus r}$ for some $r\ge1$, then $\mathcal P$ holds for $\mathcal F$; (3) for every closed immersion $i:Z\to X$ [def-weil-closed-immersion] with $Z$ an integral scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme] and every point $\xi\in X$ whose closure $\overline{\{\xi\}}$ is $i(Z)$ (the generic point of $Z$), there is a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal G$ such that (a) $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal G)=i(Z)$, (b) $\mathfrak m_\xi\mathcal G_\xi=0$, and (c) for every quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals $\mathcal J\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ with $\mathcal J_\xi=\mathcal O_{X,\xi}$ there is a coherent sub-$\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal G'\subseteq\mathcal J\mathcal G$ with $\mathcal G'_\xi=\mathcal G_\xi$ (as submodules of $\mathcal G_\xi$) such that $\mathcal P$ holds for $\mathcal G'$. Then $\mathcal P$ holds for every coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01YM (label lemma-property-higher-rank-cohomological, coherent.tex line 3425); Stacks writes 'quasi-coherent subsheaf G' of JG' in (3)(c), which on the Noetherian X is the same as a coherent one; hypothesis (0) is added here because 01YM is false without it (the property 'F is nonzero' satisfies (1)-(3) and fails for F = 0)

proof.text: (Preliminaries.) (a) On the locally Noetherian $X$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module is coherent iff it is quasi-coherent of finite type [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth]; so $\mathcal O_X$ is coherent, and kernels, cokernels and finite direct sums of maps of coherent modules, and quasi-coherent submodules and quotients of a coherent module, are coherent [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth](1),(2). The support of a coherent module is closed [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-module-support-closed]. (b) Stalks [lem-weil-pbc-module-stalk-exact]: for a sub-$\mathcal O_X$-module $\mathcal F'\subseteq\mathcal F$ the stalk $\mathcal F'_x\to\mathcal F_x$ is injective (1) and $(\mathcal F/\mathcal F')_x=\mathcal F_x/\mathcal F'_x$ (3); hence $\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal F'\subseteq\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal F$ and $\operatorname{Supp}(\mathcal F/\mathcal F')\subseteq\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal F$, and $(\mathcal F/\mathcal F')_x=0$ iff $\mathcal F'_x=\mathcal F_x$. The stalk of a finite direct sum is the direct sum of the stalks (filtered colimits commute with finite direct sums). An $\mathcal O_X$-module, or an $\mathcal O_W$-module on an open $W$, whose stalks are all $0$ is $0$, since its map to $0$ is bijective on stalks [lem-weil-pbc-module-iso-on-stalks]. (c) Let $i:Z\to X$ be a closed immersion with $Z$ integral. By definition [def-weil-closed-immersion] $i$ is a homeomorphism onto the closed subset $i(Z)$; $Z$ is irreducible [def-pc-integral-scheme], so $i(Z)$ is an irreducible closed subset of $X$; if $\eta$ is the generic point of $Z$ [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober], then $\xi=i(\eta)$ has closure $i(Z)$ and is the only point of $X$ with this closure [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-sober]. $i$ is an immersion, hence locally of finite type [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft](2), so $Z$ is locally Noetherian [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft]; thus $\mathcal O_Z$ is coherent and a sheaf of ideals of $\mathcal O_Z$ is coherent iff it is quasi-coherent (by (a) on $Z$). For a quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_Z$, $i_*\mathcal I$ is a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module with $\operatorname{Supp}(i_*\mathcal I)=i(\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal I)\subseteq i(Z)$ [lem-weil-pbc-closed-immersion-coherent-equivalence](1); and $(i_*\mathcal G)_{i(z)}\cong\mathcal G_z$ naturally in the $\mathcal O_Z$-module $\mathcal G$ [lem-weil-pbc-closed-pushforward-stalks](2). Finally $i_*$ is computed sectionwise, $(i_*\mathcal G)(V)=\mathcal G(i^{-1}V)$ [def-pc-module-pullback]: for quasi-coherent ideals $\mathcal I_1\subseteq\mathcal I_2\subseteq\mathcal O_Z$ the induced map $i_*\mathcal I_1\to i_*\mathcal I_2$ is injective on every open, and $i_*(\mathcal I^{\oplus r})=(i_*\mathcal I)^{\oplus r}$.

proof.text: (Filtrations and isomorphisms.) (a) $\mathcal P$ is invariant under isomorphism: if $\varphi:\mathcal F'\to\mathcal F$ is an isomorphism of coherent modules and $\mathcal P(\mathcal F)$, then $0\to0\to\mathcal F'\xrightarrow{\varphi}\mathcal F\to0$ is a short exact sequence of coherent modules whose outer terms have $\mathcal P$ by (0) and by assumption, so $\mathcal P(\mathcal F')$ by (1). (b) If a coherent $\mathcal F$ has a chain $0=\mathcal F_0\subseteq\dots\subseteq\mathcal F_m=\mathcal F$ of coherent submodules such that every $\mathcal F_j/\mathcal F_{j-1}$ (coherent by [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-kernel-cokernel-locnoeth](1)) has $\mathcal P$, then $\mathcal P(\mathcal F)$: by induction on $j$, $\mathcal P(\mathcal F_0)$ is (0), and $\mathcal P(\mathcal F_{j-1})$, $\mathcal P(\mathcal F_j/\mathcal F_{j-1})$ and the short exact sequence $0\to\mathcal F_{j-1}\to\mathcal F_j\to\mathcal F_j/\mathcal F_{j-1}\to0$ give $\mathcal P(\mathcal F_j)$ by (1).

proof.text: Call an irreducible closed subset $T\subseteq X$ [def-weil-irreducible-components] *good* if for every closed immersion $i:Z\to X$ with $Z$ integral and $i(Z)=T$ and every quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_Z$, $\mathcal P$ holds for $i_*\mathcal I$. Suppose, for a contradiction, that the set $\mathcal S$ of irreducible closed subsets of $X$ that are not good is nonempty. By [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-scheme-closed-subsets-minimal] it has a minimal element $T_0$; so every irreducible closed subset $T\subsetneq T_0$ is good. As $T_0$ is not good, fix a closed immersion $i:Z_0\to X$ with $Z_0$ integral and $i(Z_0)=T_0$, and a quasi-coherent ideal $\mathcal I_0\subseteq\mathcal O_{Z_0}$ such that $\mathcal P(i_*\mathcal I_0)$ fails. Let $\eta$ be the generic point of $Z_0$ and $\xi=i(\eta)$, so $\overline{\{\xi\}}=T_0$ (step 1(c)).

By step 2(a), $\operatorname{Supp}((i_j)_*\mathcal I_j)=i_j(Z_j)$, and $\mathcal F_j/\mathcal F_{j-1}$ is a quotient of a submodule of $\mathcal F$, so $i_j(Z_j)\subseteq\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal F\subseteq T_0$ (step 1(b)); $i_j(Z_j)

proof.text: ($\mathcal P(i_*\mathcal I')$ for $0\ne\mathcal I'\subseteq\mathcal I$.) Let $\mathcal I'\subseteq\mathcal I$ be a nonzero quasi-coherent ideal. Let $\beta:(i_*\mathcal I')^{\oplus r}\to(i_*\mathcal I)^{\oplus r}\xrightarrow{\alpha}\mathcal G$; it is injective on every open (step 1(c) and $\alpha$ injective), its source is coherent (step 1), and $Q'=\operatorname{Coker}\beta$, with quotient map $c:\mathcal G\to Q'$, is coherent (step 1(a)); $\operatorname{Ker}c=\operatorname{Im}\beta$ and $\beta$ is an isomorphism of its source onto $\operatorname{Im}\beta$. By step 2(b) and step 6, $\beta_\xi$ is bijective, so $Q'_\xi=0$; and $\operatorname{Supp}Q'\subseteq\operatorname{Supp}\mathcal G=T_0$ (step 1(b)). Let $\mathcal J=\operatorname{Ann}(Q')\subseteq\mathcal O_X$; by [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-theoretic-support](1),(4) it is a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals with $as=0$ for all local sections $a$ of $\mathcal J$ and $s$ of $Q'$. $\mathcal J_\xi=\mathcal O_{X,\xi}$: $\operatorname{Supp}Q'$ is closed (step 1(a)) and misses $\xi$, so $W'=X\setminus\operatorname{Supp}Q'$ is an open neighbourhood of $\xi$ on which all stalks of $Q'$ vanish, so $Q'|_{W'}=0$ (step 1(b)) and $1\in\operatorname{Ann}(Q')(W')$ by the definition of $\operatorname{Ann}$. Next $\mathcal J\mathcal G\subseteq\operatorname{Im}\beta$: the composite $\mathcal J\otimes_{\mathcal O_X}\mathcal G\to\mathcal G\xrightarrow{c}Q'$ sends each local section $a\otimes s$ to $a\,c(s)=0$; these sections generate the tensor product sheaf locally [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product], so the composite is $0$ and its image $\mathcal J\mathcal G$ lies in $\operatorname{Ker}c=\operatorname{Im}\beta$. By (3)(c) for $\mathcal J$ there is a coherent $\mathcal G'\subseteq\mathcal J\mathcal G$ with $\mathcal G'_\xi=\mathcal G_\xi$ and $\mathcal P(\mathcal G')$. Let $\mathcal G''=\beta^{-1}(\mathcal G')\subseteq(i_*\mathcal I')^{\oplus r}$; $\beta$ maps it isomorphically onto $\mathcal G'$, so $\mathcal G''$ is coherent with $\mathcal P(\mathcal G'')$ (step 3(a)), and $Q''=(i_*\mathcal I')^{\oplus r}/\mathcal G''$ is coherent (step 1(a)). As $\beta_\xi$ is bijective onto $\mathcal G_\xi=\mathcal G'_\xi$, $\mathcal G''_\xi$ is the whole stalk and $Q''_\xi=0$; and $\operatorname{Supp}Q''\subseteq\operatorname{Supp}(i_*\mathcal I')^{\oplus r}\subseteq T_0$ (step 1). By step 5, $\mathcal P(Q'')$. By (1) applied to $0\to\mathcal G''\to(i_*\mathcal I')^{\oplus r}\to Q''\to0$, $\mathcal P((i_*\mathcal I')^{\oplus r})$, and by (2) ($r\ge1$, step 6), $\mathcal P(i_*\mathcal I')$.

Hence we see that i_*I' satisfies P by (2)'). Stacks takes for J an ideal cutting out Supp Q' (e.g. the reduced induced structure) and J^n with J^n Q' = 0 by Lemma 01Y9; here J is the annihilator of Q', the ideal of the scheme-theoretic support (Morphisms 05JU), for which n = 1

proof.text: ($\mathcal P(i_*\mathcal I'')$ for every $\mathcal I''$; contradiction.) Let $\mathcal I''\subseteq\mathcal O_{Z_0}$ be a quasi-coherent ideal. If $\mathcal I''=0$, then $i_*\mathcal I''=0$ has $\mathcal P$ by (0). Otherwise $\mathcal I'=\mathcal I''\cap\mathcal I$ is a nonzero quasi-coherent ideal (step 2(c); $\mathcal I\ne0$ by step 6) contained in $\mathcal I$, so $\mathcal P(i_*\mathcal I')$ by step 7. The map $i_*\mathcal I'\to i_*\mathcal I''$ is injective (step 1(c)); its cokernel $Q'''$ is coherent, $Q'''_\xi=0$ by step 2(b) (applied to $\mathcal I'\subseteq\mathcal I''$) and step 1(b), and $\operatorname{Supp}Q'''\subseteq\operatorname{Supp}(i_*\mathcal I'')\subseteq T_0$. So $\mathcal P(Q''')$ by step 5 and $\mathcal P(i_*\mathcal I'')$ by (1). Taking $\mathcal I''=\mathcal I_0$ contradicts the choice of $\mathcal I_0$ in step 4. Hence $\mathcal S$ is empty: every irreducible closed subset of $X$ is good.

proof.text: (All coherent modules.) Let $\mathcal F$ be a coherent $\mathcal O_X$-module. If $\mathcal F=0$, $\mathcal P(\mathcal F)$ is (0). Otherwise take the chain of [lem-weil-pbc-coherent-filtration-integral-subschemes] with $\mathcal F_j/\mathcal F_{j-1}\cong(i_j)_*\mathcal I_j$, $\mathcal I_j$ quasi-coherent (step 1(c)). Each $i_j(Z_j)$ is an irreducible closed subset of $X$ (step 1(c)), good by step 8, so $\mathcal P((i_j)_*\mathcal I_j)$ and $\mathcal P(\mathcal F_j/\mathcal F_{j-1})$ (step 3(a)); by step 3(b), $\mathcal P(\mathcal F)$.
